message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue). Each color has numbers 0‑9 (two of each 1‑9, one 0) and four action cards: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two. Plus 4 Wild cards and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile. Turn the top card over to start the discard pile. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score **500 points** (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied at the end of each round. | | **Gameplay** | 1. Play proceeds clockwise (unless a Reverse changes direction). 2. On your turn, you must play **one** card that matches either the color, number, or symbol of the top discard. 3. If you can’t play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. | | **Wild Draw Four Rules** | You may only play it if you have **no other playable card** (i.e., you cannot match the current color or number). If challenged and you were wrong, you must draw 4 cards instead of the opponent drawing 4. | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards remaining in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, action cards = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches the target score (usually 500). | | **Variations** | • **Stacking** – allow players to stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards on each other.
• **Custom rules** – e.g., “Draw Two” can be played on any card, or “Reverse” acts like a Skip. Always agree on variations before starting. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of the current color** – even after a Wild, remember the chosen color for the next turn. 2. **Plan ahead** – try to hold onto action cards for strategic moments. 3. **Watch opponents** – if someone is close to UNO, be ready to challenge a Wild Draw Four. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
